info.title: ControlClaw firewall panel API
info.description: The local panel's API on a standalone firewall (docs/standalone/panel-api.md). Sign in with POST /api/login; every write sends the session's CSRF token as x-csrf-token.

post.summary: Set the admin's password with the setup token from the log
Sign in

post.summary: Change the admin's password; every other session is signed out
Sign out

The identity map
The last 100 permission requests

get.summary: The latest activity rows

Run a firewall command by name (actions scoped "both")

post.summary: Add an egress rule
Move a rule to its next effect: allow, ask, block, allow

get.summary: Activity rows by kind and verdict, newest first, with the counts

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Which log: `network` is traffic and what the firewall decided about messages and webhooks.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Words to find in the row's text, at most 200 characters.

parameters.name: routine
parameters.description:
Show routine traffic too: what the rules for model keys and bots let through with the key the
firewall put in (`ROUTINE`). Hidden when left out, unless `q` is given.

get.summary: The overview: the cards, the traffic chart, the live list, top hosts, agents and AI findings
The traffic chart for a range
The newest requests (at most 50), after a cursor

parameters.name: afterId
parameters.description: `id` of the newest row the list holds: only rows after it.

get.summary: The pairing codes still waiting, without the codes
Where agents' machines reach this firewall's pairing endpoint, when it knows
Permission requests, newest first (at most 200)

parameters.description: Only these; all when left out.

post.summary: Approve or deny a pending request

Who may email the agents and whom they may email, and held mail (`email.read`)

parameters.description: Remove it even when its agent cannot be told. The agent keeps a stand-in that no longer works.

get.summary: The AgentMail account and its inboxes (`agentmail.read`)

post.summary: An AgentMail action: signup, claim, check, create, import, attach, senders, forget, delete, push. The body is the action's (`cc-contracts` agentmail); `vmId` is filled in with the agent's name and address.

Read the logins from 1Password again
Disconnect 1Password

SetupBody.description: `POST /api/setup`: the first admin, with the token from the log.

SignedIn.description: `POST /api/setup` and `/api/login`: the session cookie is set; writes send `csrf` back.

setup.description: No admin yet: set one up with the token from the log.

csrf.description: The session's CSRF token, when signed in.

PasswordBody.description: `POST /api/admin/password`: the current password, and a new one of at least 12 characters.

signedOut.description: How many other sessions were ended.

PasswordChanged.description: The password is changed; every other session is ended, this one stays.

CommandAnswer.description: A command handler's outcome, as the firewall gives it (`CommandOutcome`).

managed.description:
Set on a rule this firewall added by itself for a model key (`anthropic`, `openai`, …) or a
bot (`telegram`, `slack`): it cannot be changed, and goes when the key or the bot does.

Exit.description: Where a rule's traffic leaves from. `residential` goes through the exit proxy (Settings).

exitCountry.description: Two letters, for a residential exit.

priority.description: 0 to 1,000,000; lower runs first. 1000 when left out.

vmId.description: One agent's rule; every agent's when left out.

aiPolicy.description: At most 1000 characters: instructions on an allow rule, the approval policy on an ask rule.

EgressRulePatch.description: Each field left out stays as it is; `null` clears one that may be empty.

NoBody.description: The `{}` body of a write that takes nothing.

oneOf.description: Let through, and logged (and read by the AI log review when it is on).

DefaultEffect.description: "Every other site": what happens to a request no rule matches.

credentials.description: The model keys the review can use.

active.description: The firewall has the settings: on, with a key it holds.

enabled.description: The AI firewall: the check on each request, AI approval, and the content rules' AI.

logReviewEnabled.description: AI log review: the review every minute and the scan.

requestInstructions.description: Left out: unchanged; `null` or empty: none. At most 2000 characters.

id.description: The firewall's credential id; the AI review settings name it.

state.description: `active`, or `failed` when the firewall did not take it.

reviewModel.description: The AI review can use this provider; its suggested model.

replace.description: Replace the provider's key; without it, a provider that has one is refused (409).

provider.description: A provider with a key here (`GET /api/llm/keys`).

model.description: OpenClaw's id for the model, with its provider: `openrouter/moonshotai/kimi-k2`.

counts.description: For the verdict tabs, whatever the verdict filter.

routine.description: Routine requests left out of the rows and the counts (0 when they are shown).

agent.description: The agent's name, or null for the firewall's own.

status.description: The status as the box sent it (the rule's effect for traffic).

statusCode.description: Traffic only: the upstream's HTTP status.

rule.description: Traffic only: the rule that decided it.

hours.description: The hour starts of the cards' series: the last 24, oldest first.

value.description: Requests in the last full minute.

today.description: Today so far, and yesterday up to the same time.

series.description: One value per hour, oldest first, matching `hours`.

today.description: Today so far, and yesterday up to the same time.

series.description: One value per hour, oldest first, matching `hours`.

value.description: Median ms of allowed requests in the last hour; null with none.

long.description: A tunnel or a request over 25 s.

vmId.description: Null for the firewall's own traffic.

hourly.description: Requests per hour over the last 24 hours.

name.description: The agent's name on the firewall; the machine's own name when left out.

ttl_minutes.description: How long the code works: 10 minutes by default, at most 60.

address.description:
The IPv4 address the proxy will see the machine at, when it is not the one pairing comes
from (a NAT, a reverse proxy, a container on the firewall's machine).

replace.description: Whether the machine may take the place of an agent already at its address.

NewCodeBody.description: What the admin says about the machine the code is for.

PendingCode.description: A code still waiting, without the code.

open.description: `false` with `PAIR_BIND=off`: this firewall takes no pairings.

port.description: The pairing port (`PAIR_BIND`'s, 8801 by default); `null` when closed.

url.description:
On the firewall's network: the proxy's host (`PAIR_PROXY_ADDR`, which install.sh writes
from `--listen`) and the pairing port. `null` when the firewall does not know it.

remoteUrl.description: From another network, over WireGuard's public address (`WG_ENDPOINT`), when that differs.

PairAddress.description: The address `controlclaw connect --firewall` takes, from what the firewall was set up with.

detail.description: Label and value pairs, as the box sent them.

externalId.description: The box's own id for it.

change.description: The module's change, as `cc-contracts` types it.

draft.description: The rule being edited, tried as if saved.

kill.description: The firewall's own account: `{org, agents: [{vmId, ...}]}`; null when it has none.

vmId.description: One agent; every agent when left out.

key.description: The key set, or null: agents use the free search.

residential.description:
The firewall's own account: provider, host, sticky, cap, country, bytes used, last check;
`{configured: false}` when there is none.

providerName.description: The name shown in the summary; the provider id when left out.

usernameTemplate.description: How the proxy's user name is written, with `{username}`, `{session}`, `{country}`.

country.description: Two letters; any country when left out.

codeRecipients.description: The firewall's own account of who gets codes (`code_recipients`): approved and allowed senders.

approvedSenders.description: People approved to talk to it.

appToken.description: Slack only: the app-level token (socket mode).

vmId.description: The agent it answers for; none yet when left out.

code.description: The code the bot sent the person (4 to 16 characters).

senderId.description: The person's id on the channel.

service.description: The app's id in the catalog (`github`, `linear`, ...).

serviceName.description: Its name, for the summary; the id when left out.

extra.description: Fields that are not secret (an account's domain, a region).

vmIds.description: The agents that may use it.

clientId.description: Your own OAuth app, when the app needs one: its client id and secret.

extra.description: Other fields of your OAuth app (a tenant, a domain).

authorizationOptionIds.description: The permissions asked for, by the setup's option ids.

name.description: Lower case letters, digits and dashes, at most 40: how agents name it.

clientId.description: OAuth: your own client, when the server does not register one itself.

vmIds.description: The agents that get it once it is connected.

sites.description: The sites it may be used on.

vmIds.description: The agents that may use it.

mode.description: `swap` (the proxy puts the password in) or `type` (the firewall types it into the page).
